subject: Performance triage: Petrichor private cluster — rising tail latency & 502s
messages:
From: Alex Sreedhar <alex.sreedhar@petrichor.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Amy Chen <amy.chen@petrichor.ai>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: High tail latency and intermittent 502s on private cluster

Sofia,

We're seeing a sustained increase in p95 latency for our embeddings and short-text generation endpoints on our private VPC deployment (cluster: petrichor-prod-1). Baseline p95 is usually ~120-180ms; over the last 45 minutes p95 is ~1.2s and 502s are at ~2.4% of requests. Error traces point to decoder timeouts and occasional OOMs on the worker processes.

What we've observed so far:
- Spike coincides with a traffic surge from a scheduled nightly batch (larger seq lengths than typical).
- Model: open-instruct-v1.2-quant (int8) pinned to runtime build r2026-05-10.
- Temporary mitigations tried by our SRE: reduced max_concurrency from 24 -> 8, bumped replica count +1, restarted a subset of workers (no durable improvement).

Attached are a perf snapshot and a small extract of the decoder logs. This is impacting inference for paying customers (severe degradation for a subset of requests). We need Redwood ops on this immediately — Petrichor leadership is watching and expects an ETA for mitigation within 2 hours.

Attachments: perf-snapshot-20260619.json (perf counters), decode-tail.log.txt (last 500 lines)

Please advise next steps and whether you need us to pause the nightly batch.

— Alex

Subject: Re: High tail latency and intermittent 502s on private cluster

Laura / Markus — Alex from Petrichor is reporting a rising p95 (~1.2s) and ~2.4% 502s on their private cluster (petrichor-prod-1). They've already scaled replicas and throttled concurrency without improvement. Customer is requesting ETA within 2 hours and leadership (CTO Amy Chen) is on the thread.

Immediate asks:
1) Can infra confirm whether this is a KV-cache growth / memory fragmentation issue vs decoder kernel mismatch? Alex attached perf snapshot and logs (see attachments).
2) If it's a kernel choice issue for the int8 runtime, can we roll a temporary kernel pin or fallback to the previous runtime build?
3) If mitigation requires a rolling restart, we need an estimated duration and customer-facing mitigation message.

I'm standing up a quick triage call in 20 mins to capture findings and decide if we escalate to CS + Execs. Please prioritize — Petrichor is a mid-enterprise customer on a reserved private plan (see deal RDW-98721).

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 10:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Performance triage: Petrichor private cluster — rising tail latency & 502s

Sofia — quick update from the runtime triage (notes below and attached triage-notes-20260619.md):

Summary of findings:
- Heap growth on decoder workers tracked to KV-cache retention: the nightly batch is sending long prefix sequences (~2048 tokens) for reranking; KV entries are not being evicted aggressively, which causes GPU memory pressure during decoding.
- Simultaneously, we see the optimized kernel selector choosing a mixed-precision int8 kernel path that underperforms for these particular sequence shapes (longer context + dynamic attention). That path is incurring CPU-side fallback work which increases end-to-end latency.
- A small subset of workers hit CUDA OOM and returned 502s while the autoscaler provisioned replacements.

Immediate remediation options (ranked):
A) Evict prefix/KV aggressively for user batch sessions older than 120s + enable per-request max_cache_entries=128 (customer-visible config) — LOW RISK, immediate, should lower memory pressure.
B) Pin model runtime to previous kernel selection (r2026-04-28 kernels) for that cluster only — MEDIUM RISK, needs quick rollout (rolling restart of 6 workers), estimate 45-60 minutes.
C) Temporarily block the nightly batch or throttle it to reduce peak concurrent long-context requests — CUSTOMER ACTIONABLE (we need Petrichor to agree).

Recommended next steps for the 0-2 hour window:
- Apply (A) on petrichor-prod-1 now (I can push the config change to the cluster in ~12 minutes).
- If A improves but not enough, schedule (B) as a targeted rollback for the cluster (45–60m) and notify Petrichor.

I've attached a short kernel selector diff and a small log snippet (decode-tail.log.txt) showing the OOM traces.

-- Markus
Markus Klein
Senior Software Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 14:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Petrichor private cluster — mitigation plan and exec note draft

Team — following Markus's triage, we've implemented the KV eviction policy change (per Markus (A)) and pushed max_cache_entries=128. Early telemetry shows p95 improved from ~1.2s -> ~420ms over the last 18 minutes and 502s down to 0.6%. We'll continue monitoring for the next hour.

Customer communication suggested (short):
- Thank you for the patience — we identified aggressive KV retention + an unfavorable kernel selection for long-context decode as the root cause. We've applied a config mitigation which reduced memory pressure and improved tail latency. We're preparing a targeted kernel pin rollback to fully restore prior p95 behavior; ETA for that rollback is ~60 minutes if needed.

Action items for execs / CS:
- Marissa: recommend a 10% service credit offer if the kernel rollback is required and we cause a >30m interruption during the targeted rollout.
- Karthik: please prepare a 1‑page brief for Petrichor CTO Amy Chen summarizing root cause, our short-term mitigation, and the plan/ETA for the targeted kernel rollout. Attach the triage notes and perf snapshot.
- Sofia: please coordinate with Alex/Amy on whether they can pause the nightly batch if rollback is needed.

I'll keep this thread updated. If metrics regress we will escalate to a cross-functional incident bridge and loop in execs for a customer call.

Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Operations — Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com
